claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I do. I'm inquiring about my son Alex. He's 20 and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I need to ask you some questions about Alex to determine eligibility.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?**

(This is important because Child Benefit can continue for children under 20 if they're in approved education or training, but generally stops at age 16 otherwise.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any education or training at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have a few more questions:

**Is Alex currently working, and if so, how many hours per week does he work?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't work at all currently.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Let me ask:

**Is Alex registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services?**

(This is relevant because if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training and registers with a careers service or armed services, Child Benefit can continue for up to 20 weeks. However, I need to clarify Alex's situation as he's 20.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not registered with any careers service or the armed services.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. I have a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

**When did Alex turn 20, or is he still 19?**

(I need to confirm his exact age, as Child Benefit eligibility generally ends when a young person turns 20, even if they're in approved education or training.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's 20 - he turned 20 earlier this year.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. Just a couple more questions to complete my assessment:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. One final question:

**Are you currently receiving Child Benefit for Alex, or are you looking to make a new claim?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm looking to make a new claim - I haven't been claiming it before.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry, but based on the information you've provided, **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why: Child Benefit is normally available for children under 16. For young people aged 16 or over, Child Benefit can continue until they turn 20, but **only if** they stay in approved education or training.

Since Alex is already 20 years old (having turned 20 earlier this year), he has exceeded the maximum age limit for Child Benefit eligibility. Unfortunately, even though he lives at home with you and is not currently working, Child Benefit cannot be claimed for anyone aged 20 or older, regardless of their circumstances.

If Alex were to enter approved education or training in the future, he would still be over the age limit, so this wouldn't change the outcome.

Is there anything else I can help you with regarding benefits?
